verses.1: In the twenty-second year of King Ahaz of Judah, King Hoshea son of Elah was king over Israel for six years.
verses.2: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, but not like the kings of Israel who came before him.
verses.3: On him rose Shalmaneser, king of Assyria. He became his servant, and he was given a place to rest.
verses.4: And the king of Assyria found a scroll in Hosh’a Keshar. This scroll contained instructions for sending servants to Soma, the king of Egypt. But he never brought any gifts to the king of Assyria, year after year. So the king of Assyria imprisoned him and kept him in prison.
verses.5: And King Ashur rose up over all the land. Shomer also rose up, and he spent three years building it.
verses.6: In the ninth year of the reign of Hoshea, king of Assyria, he took control of Shomeran. He freed Israel from Assyrian rule. He settled them in the cities along the banks of the Gozan River.
verses.7: And it happened that when the children of Israel sinned against their God, who had brought them out of Egypt from the hands of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. They became afraid of other gods instead.
verses.8: And they followed the laws of those nations, which Jehovah decreed from before the children of Israel and the kings of Israel.
verses.9: And the children of Israel sinned against God. They did things that were not right in His eyes. They built altars in every city, from the highest hills to the lowest valleys.
verses.10: And they set up their shelters, and they lived on every high ground and under every tree.
verses.11: And there they were destroyed in every way, along with all those nations that Jehovah had banished from their lands. They did evil deeds, in order to provoke Jehovah’s anger.
verses.12: And the Gibeals obeyed what Jehovah said: “Do not do this.”
verses.13: And Jehovah determined that in Israel and in Judah, all the prophets and seers would say, “Turn away from your evil ways! Obey my laws and commandments, just as I commanded your ancestors. I sent my servants, the prophets, to you.”
verses.14: And they did not listen, and they became like their ancestors, who did not believe in their God.
verses.15: And they broke their laws and their covenant, which they had made with their ancestors. They also broke the promises they had made to them. They followed the darkness, and they became lost in it. They also went after the nations around them, even though Jehovah had commanded them not to do such things.
verses.16: They broke all of Yahweh’s commands. They made idols out of two golden calves. They worshiped all the heavenly beings. They served those idols instead of Yahweh.
verses.17: And they would carry their sons and daughters into the fire. They would put on spells on them, and they would be sold as slaves to do evil deeds in the eyes of Jehovah, so that He would be angry.
verses.18: And Jehovah became very angry with Israel. He removed them from His presence; not a single tribe of Judah remained at all.
verses.19: Even the Jews did not keep the commandments of Jehovah their God. They followed the laws of Israel, which they had established.
verses.20: And Jehovah punished every one of Israel’s descendants. He handed them over to the Philistines until they were completely destroyed by them.
verses.21: For Israel broke away from the house of David. Yeravam, son of Nebat, became their king. But Yeravam drove Israel away from God’s side. They committed a great sin.
verses.22: And the children of Israel went through all those sins that Rehoboam had committed.
verses.23: Until Jehovah removes Israel from his face, as it is written in all the words of His prophets. Israel will be destroyed from its land, and Assyria will rule over it until today.
verses.24: And the king of Assyria came from Babylon, from Kutha, from Avuah, from Hamat, and from Sefarvaim. He settled in the cities of Samaria, under the rule of the Israelites. They took over Samaria and settled there.
verses.25: At the beginning of their Sabbath, they did not fear Jehovah. Therefore, Jehovah sent storms upon them, and they were killed.
verses.26: And they said to the king of Assyria, “The nations that you have exiled and taken captive to the cities of Shomron do not know the laws of the God of the earth. Therefore, He has sent storms upon them, and they are killed because they do not know the laws of the God of the earth.”
verses.27: And the king of Assyria commanded, “Let one of the priests who were taken there be brought back. They shall go there and sit down, and then they shall carry out the judgment of the God of the land.”
verses.28: And one of the priests who had been released from their prison came and sat in the house of God. He became angry with them, saying, “How can they fear Jehovah?”
verses.29: And various nations became his people. They were placed in the houses of worship that the priests built for them in their own cities where they lived.
verses.30: And the people of Babylon made weapons out of metal. The people of Kuth made spears. And the people of Hamat made axes.
verses.31: And the Ammonites did what they were ordered to do. They burned their children in fire, in Adrameychel and Ananemelach, the gods of the Ammonites.
verses.32: And they became afraid of Jehovah. They appointed priests for the sacrifices, and they worked in the house of sacrifice.
verses.33: They would fear Jehovah, and they would worship their gods, just as the nations did when they were brought out of those places.
verses.34: Until today, they continue to act according to those old laws. They do not fear Jehovah, nor do they follow His laws, statutes, and commands. These are the laws that Jehovah commanded His descendants, the descendants of Jacob, who named Israel after Him.
verses.35: And Jehovah made a covenant with them. He commanded them, “Do not fear other gods. Do not worship them, do not serve them, and do not offer them any sacrifices.”
verses.36: For Jehovah, who has brought you up from the land of Egypt by His great power and mighty hand, you must fear Him, worship Him, and serve Him.
verses.37: And these laws, and these regulations, and these commandments that were written for you, you must keep them all the days of your life. Do not fear other gods.
verses.38: And the covenant that I have made with you, do not forget it. Do not fear other gods.
verses.39: For if you fear Jehovah your God, He will save you from all your enemies.
verses.40: And they did not listen, because their first judgment was what they did.
verses.41: And these nations would fear Jehovah. Their ancestors also obeyed His commands. And their descendants continue to do so to this day.
